title: Introduce lightweight Rust+WASM mini-RAG worker + deterministic eval harness
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Provide a minimal, production-minded example that shows how to build a compact RAG-style worker in Rust, compile it to WebAssembly for lightweight edge deployment, and wire up deterministic evals and snapshot assertions so teams can iterate safely. Many existing quickstarts target JS/TS; this PR demonstrates a low-footprint alternative for constrained runtimes and for teams preferring Rust ergonomics.

What this PR adds (high level): 1) examples/rust-wasm-minirag/: a minimal Rust worker that accepts tool-call stubs and demonstrates a simple retrieval + prompt template flow; 2) examples/rust-wasm-minirag/devcontainer/ and README with step-by-step local dev instructions (cargo + wasm-pack + wasm-bindgen); 3) a deterministic eval harness (examples/rust-wasm-minirag/eval/) based on snapshot assertions and seeded RNG for stable outputs across CI runs; 4) a compact telemetry probe shim that emits structured debug events (span-like) to stdout so the quickstart can be hooked into the Console demo dashboards; 5) docs/quickstarts/rust-wasm-minirag.md added to the docs site content tree with usage, security considerations, and recommended rollout steps.

Compatibility & scope: This quickstart is intentionally small — it uses a toy in-memory index and stubbed tool-calls to highlight integration patterns (tool binding, structured output contracts, streaming outline). It is not a full production indexer. However the telemetry and snapshot-based eval approaches are intended to be copy-pasteable into larger services.

Developer notes & runbook (single-string): Clone repo -> cd examples/rust-wasm-minirag -> make dev (devcontainer provided) -> wasm-pack build && npm run serve-local -> run eval harness with `cargo run --bin eval-runner -- --seed 42` to check snapshots. See README for cargo toolchain pins and wasm-bindgen versions.

Testing: added unit tests for the prompt templater and a deterministic scenario runner used by the snapshot harness. CI adds a new lightweight workflow (ci/workflows/rust-wasm-quickstart.yml) that runs cargo test, wasm-pack build, and the eval harness. Initial CI run failed due to a missing wasm-bindgen feature; fixed in commit 3.

Docs site updates: docs/quickstarts/rust-wasm-minirag.md contains the quickstart narrative, security considerations for WASM sandboxes, recommended telemetry knobs in Console, and a short checklist for migrating the example to Redwood Dedicated or Private (notes on pinning model variants and KMS usage).

Related: reuses telemetry schema fields introduced in ENG-1765 and references the eval snapshot format from ENG-1902.

review_thread: Luis Ortega: Nice example — can we avoid serde_json in the wasm path to reduce binary size? (suggestion: use minimal serde feature set)
Maya Chen: Good point — removed default serde features and switched to serde-derive with alloc feature. Confirmed size delta locally (~80KB smaller).
Devon Patel: Eval harness looks solid. Two requests: (1) add a short negative test for a malformed tool response, (2) document expected snapshot update process in the README.
Maya Chen: Added negative scenario and an appendix in the README explaining `cargo eval --update-snapshots` flow and safety notes.
Rohit Mehra: CI failed first run — saw wasm-bindgen missing feature. After the fix CI passed on re-run. Approved.
Automated CI: First run (linux/cargo): fail — missing wasm-bindgen feature. Rerun: pass. Lint: pass. wasm-pack: pass. Eval harness: pass.
release_notes: Add Rust+WASM mini-RAG quickstart with deterministic evals and telemetry probe shim. Useful for edge/low-footprint deployments and for teams preferring Rust toolchains.
